name: The Goring Hotel
positioning: Family-run Belgravia hotel built in 1910, a short stroll from Buckingham Palace, with a large private garden and footman service
best_for: Royal-history enthusiasts who want a Belgravia base near Buckingham Palace
Families wanting interconnecting garden-view suites and children's activities

facts.text: The Goring was built in 1910 by its founder, Otto Goring.
The hotel is on a Belgravia street, a 10-minute stroll from Buckingham Palace.
Victoria station is a five-minute walk from the hotel.
Guests can play croquet in the garden.
Belgravia Suites have a marble fireplace, historic silks and hand-crafted walnut furniture.
Garden Family Suites have interconnecting rooms, entertainment for children and garden views.
Conde Nast Traveler says The Goring was the world's first hotel with central heating and en suite bathrooms in every room.
Kate Middleton spent the night before her 2011 wedding to Prince William at the hotel.
Children receive The Goring Passport and can decorate desserts in the kitchen.
Footmen in red tailcoats and gold-trimmed waistcoats look after guests.
Afternoon Tea is served on The Veranda, which overlooks the garden.
The Dining Room walls are covered in monkeys drinking Champagne or bursting out of cakes.

highlights.text: The hotel says it owns London's largest private garden, behind the hotel.
The Royal Suite has a life-size portrait of Queen Victoria, letters handwritten by royalty and the same silk as Buckingham Palace's Throne Room.
Guests in a Belgravia Suite, the Royal Suite or a Garden Suite have a dedicated footman.
The hotel has passed down through four generations of the Goring family.
Teddy, a Shetland pony, is the hotel pet.

considerations.text: The Dining Room dress code requests no sportswear, athletic trainers, shorts or ripped jeans.
WhataHotel notes the traditional decor may feel formal for some guests.
WhataHotel notes premium pricing reflecting the luxury positioning.
